findings.description: The phase aggregate `aggregate.cost_usd` (1.0008492080000001) is not the exact sum of the per-task `cost_usd` values it claims to sum. The exact sum of the eleven per-subagent `execution.cost_usd` values in docs/implementation/17.1..17.4/orchestration.json is 1.0008492599999999 (per-task subtotals 17.1 = 0.26487149399999999, 17.2 = 0.16841078400000004, 17.3 = 0.15843295199999996, 17.4 = 0.40913402999999998), a discrepancy of 5.2e-8. The aggregate's own note lists the same values and states '= 1.000849208', which is itself arithmetically off by 5.2e-8. This is materially smaller than the phase-16 P16-F2 mismatch (0.0295) and is an advisory metric only, with no functional or gate impact; the other aggregate fields are consistent (task_count 4, review_rounds 5, rework_rounds 1, subagent_invocations 11).
findings.detail: The aggregate JSON uses rounded values for two of the 17.4 subagents (worker attempt 1 as 0.122437506 vs the file's 0.12243750599999997, reviewer attempt 1 as 0.036446382 vs 0.036446381999999986), which does not by itself explain a 5.2e-8 gap (double-precision rounding at magnitude ~1 is ~2.2e-16). The stated figure and the note's sum are both a small mis-add of the listed values.
evidence: Independent awk sum of the four task files = 1.0008492599999999
findings.recommended_action: Reconcile the aggregate `cost_usd` against the per-task records (or state the basis if an invocation outside the four task files is intended). Advisory metric only; no functional impact.

findings.description: The diagnostics panel's well-formed-but-wrong-shape-object fallback path has no structural test. `PageFailsClosedWhenTheRequestIsRejectedOrTheBodyIsMalformed` only covers the null / non-object / array guard, the rejection clear, and the caught-exception clear; there is no case for a well-formed JSON object of an unexpected or partial shape (for example `{}` or `{"QueueDepth":5}`), which the shipped code renders as the full fixed 28-row table with 0/`Unknown` fallback values (config.html:595-641, 568-593). The security review SR-17.4-01 recommended option (a) tighten the wording 'and add a structural test for the wrong-shape-object case either way'; the attempt-2 correction chose option (a) documentation-only and did not add the test (recorded by the 17.4 reviewer as I1). The behaviour is deliberate, documented, and non-security-relevant (no free-form text, no secret, no error surface), so this is a bounded coverage residual rather than a defect.
findings.detail: The corrected documentation (README.md:148-151, architecture 11/12, archive F3, ADR-025 implementation note) now accurately describes the fallback table, so the documentation claim and the code agree. The gap is solely that the fallback rendering is pinned by prose rather than by an executable structural assertion over the embedded page text.
evidence: src/ArrTags/Configuration/config.html:595-600 (object-only guard) and 568-593 (0/'Unknown' bounded readers) and 641 (panel shown for any other object)
findings.recommended_action: Add a structural test asserting the wrong-shape-object ('{}') fallback table rendering and visibility, or explicitly accept the prose-only pin in the limitation register. Not required for the phase gate.

findings.description: The shipped code comment at src/ArrTags/Configuration/config.html:512-514 still states that 'a rejected, unauthorized, unavailable, or malformed response leaves no data'. After the SR-17.4-01 correction the canonical documentation distinguishes an unparseable or non-object response (panel cleared, fail-closed) from a well-formed but unexpected or partial-shape object (fixed table with 0/'Unknown' fallback), so the comment is now less precise than the documentation and than the shipped behaviour for the wrong-shape case. It is a code comment only: not user-visible, not persisted, and not a claim the project ships. The 17.4 worker attempt 2 and reviewer attempt 2 recorded it as an out-of-scope residual because the delegated correction was documentation-only and prohibited production-code changes.
findings.detail: The comment is accurate for a genuinely unparseable or non-object body; it overstates only for the well-formed wrong-shape object, which the corrected documentation now covers. Aligning it requires a one-line code-comment edit outside Phase 17 scope.
evidence: README.md:146-153; docs/architecture/11-failure-consistency-and-security-policy.md:63-68; docs/architecture/12-performance-and-operational-limits.md:192-199; docs/limitations/archive.md:202-210; docs/decisions/ADR-025.md:107-113 (the corrected, qualified wording)
findings.recommended_action: Optionally align the code comment with the qualified documentation wording in a future code change; not required for the phase gate.

findings.description: The two F3 live-verification bounds are genuine and correctly disclosed rather than overclaimed. (1) The panel's inline JavaScript is not executed by the suite or the pinned live matrix (no JavaScript runtime in the repository; the pinned host runs `--nowebclient`), so the panel is verified structurally against the endpoint model and the pinned jellyfin-web source; this is registered as accepted limitation V12-F3-1. (2) The host-guarded fact `EndpointUsesThePinnedHostAdministratorGatingPolicy` is skipped here because `ARRTAGS_JELLYFIN_HOST_DIR` is unset, so the live host-side AuthorizationMiddleware path is not confirmed; the in-process MVC pipeline instead reproduces 401/403/200 and the pinned host policy definition was read from source. The v1.2 plan assigns the live endpoint/panel verification to Phase 21 task 21.4; that matrix runs `--nowebclient` (which does not affect the server-side endpoint authorization but does mean it will not execute the panel JS). The process-lifetime semantics are disclosed in ADR-025, the archive entry, README, and the changelog.
findings.detail: Both bounds are stated in the ADR-025 implementation note, the F3 archive verification-bounds paragraph, the task 17.4 changelog entry, and V12-F3-1. The endpoint authorization residual is a legitimate host-environment boundary; the F3 acceptance criterion's 'host-guarded confirmation' is therefore not yet demonstrated live, only structurally plus in-process, and remains satisfiable at Phase 21.4.
findings.recommended_action: No action for Phase 17; carry the live endpoint/panel check into Phase 21 task 21.4.

summary: Phase 17 (Goal F3, ADR-025) is complete and Gate 17 is met: all four tasks 17.1-17.4 have reviewed commits, worker/reviewer evidence, and per-task orchestration records, and the phase aggregate exists with gate_status PENDING_PHASE_REVIEW. Independent inspection confirms the shipped code matches the ADR-025 contract and the canonical documents: ArrTagsStatusController is a class-level [Authorize(Policy = Policies.RequiresElevation)] GET-only route with no [AllowAnonymous] and no write verb, returning the fixed-shape DiagnosticsSnapshot (nine top-level fields / 28 leaf paths: queue depth and in-flight, Sonarr/Radarr ArrConnectionHealth, three MediaMatchStatus failure classifications, cache hits/misses, 18 RenderFailureReason classifications, and stale-metadata transitions); the model graph carries only int/long/bounded enums (the tests pin the 28-leaf serialized shape and the two enum string leaves), so no secret, path, item name, identifier list, provider payload, or unbounded collection can be serialized, and the counters are recorded only at existing bounded boundaries (verified in code and by the instrumentation tests). The read-only panel on the anonymous settings page is static-hidden and empty until a bounded snapshot renders, uses only fixed literals plus the bounded numeric/enum readers via textContent, and clears on rejection or an unparseable/non-object body; it adds no input, settings field, or save wiring. Metrics are wired into all instrumentation sites through the plugin DI registrator, and the integration-boundary tests (endpoint pipeline 401/403/200, panel structure, snapshot shape, instrumentation at each boundary) are meaningful and non-vacuous. The clause 6 security review is PASS_WITH_FINDINGS with no open BLOCKER/HIGH: SR-17.4-01 is genuinely closed by the attempt-2 documentation-precision correction (the unconditional 'malformed' wording is gone from all five documentation surfaces and the 0/'Unknown' fallback is stated), and SR-17.4-02 is closed by the correctly registered accepted limitation V12-F3-1 (accepted.md, 00-index.md, state.json). F3 is recorded resolved (open.md removed, archive.md resolution, 00-index Resolved, state.json limitations, status.md regenerated), the honest verification bounds (panel JS not executed; host-guarded authorization fact skipped; process-lifetime counters) are disclosed, the build and full default suite reproduce Failed 0 / Passed 1794 / Skipped 64 / Total 1858, and check-docs.sh and render-docs-state --check pass. Phase 17 remains PLANNED with gate Gate 17 / tag v1.2.0-phase17 and no tag applied, as required before the orchestrator's gate step. No BLOCKER or HIGH is open. Three LOW findings are recorded as non-blocking residuals: the aggregate cost figure is not the exact sum of the per-task records (P17-F1, ~5.2e-8), the wrong-shape-object panel fallback has no structural test (P17-F2), and the config.html code comment retains the pre-correction wording (P17-F3); none affects correctness, security, or the gate. Verdict: APPROVED_WITH_FINDINGS; phase complete and ready for the next phase.
